note: The first-party drink list: every drink on the IBA's three category pages (The Unforgettables, Contemporary Classics, New Era) that could be read from its own page on iba-world.com. Names and standard proportions are referenced (© IBA, all rights reserved); the instruction text and every translation are ours. Nothing here is recalled: each recipe was read, and the ones that could not be are not in the list. Barracuda is deliberately absent: the IBA removed it in 2024 (it.wikipedia, 'Estromissione = 2024', citing the AIBM Project's IBA Official Cocktails 2024), which is why its iba-world.com page now 404s and the English Wikipedia article carries no official recipe.

recipes.name: Alexander
methodSteps: Shake the three in a shaker with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Grate nutmeg over the top.

recipes.name: Americano
methodSteps: Build the two over ice in an old-fashioned glass.
Top with a splash of soda.
Stir once, and garnish.

recipes.name: Aviation
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a cherry.

recipes.name: Bee's Knees
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Bellini
methodSteps: Pour the purée into a chilled flute.
Add the prosecco slowly and stir once.

recipes.name: Black Russian
methodSteps: Pour the two over ice in an old-fashioned glass.
Stir briefly.

recipes.name: Bloody Mary
methodSteps: Roll everything between two tins rather than shaking it.
Strain into a highball over ice.
Garnish with celery.

recipes.name: Boulevardier
methodSteps: Stir the three over ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.name: Angel Face
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Between the Sheets
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Twist a lemon peel over the top.

recipes.name: Brandy Crusta
methodSteps: Rim a wine glass with sugar and set a wide lemon peel inside it.
Shake the rest with ice.
Strain into the glass.

recipes.name: Casino
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a lemon twist and a cherry.

recipes.name: Clover Club
methodSteps: Shake first without ice, to lift the white.
Shake again with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Daiquiri
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Dry Martini
methodSteps: Stir over ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with an olive or a lemon twist.

recipes.name: Gin Fizz
methodSteps: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into a highball and top with soda.
Garnish with a lemon slice.

recipes.name: Hanky Panky
methodSteps: Stir the three over ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.name: John Collins
methodSteps: Build the gin, lemon and syrup over ice in a highball.
Top with soda and stir once.
Garnish with a lemon slice and a cherry.

recipes.name: Last Word
methodSteps: Shake the four in equal parts with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Manhattan
methodSteps: Stir over ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a cherry.

recipes.name: Martinez
methodSteps: Stir everything over ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.name: Mary Pickford
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a cherry.

recipes.name: Monkey Gland
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.name: Negroni
methodSteps: Build the three over ice in a lowball.
Stir once.
Garnish with an orange slice.

recipes.name: Caipirinha
methodSteps: Cut the lime into wedges and put them in a lowball with the sugar.
Muddle, then fill with ice and add the cachaça.
Stir.

recipes.name: Champagne Cocktail
methodSteps: Put the sugar cube in a chilled flute and soak it with the bitters.
Add the cognac, then the champagne.
Stir once.

recipes.name: Corpse Reviver #2
methodSteps: Rinse a chilled cocktail glass with absinthe and discard the rest.
Shake the other four with ice.
Strain into the glass.

recipes.name: Cosmopolitan
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.name: Cuba Libre
methodSteps: Squeeze the lime into a highball over ice and drop it in.
Add the rum, then the cola.
Stir once.

recipes.name: French 75
methodSteps: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into a chilled flute.
Top with champagne and stir once.

recipes.name: French Connection
methodSteps: Pour the two over ice in a lowball.
Stir once.

recipes.name: Garibaldi
methodSteps: Build the Campari over ice in a highball.
Add the orange juice.
Whip it briefly so the juice froths, and stir.

recipes.name: Grasshopper
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a mint leaf.

recipes.name: Hemingway Special
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Horse's Neck
methodSteps: Cut a long strip of lemon peel and hang it inside a highball.
Add ice and the cognac.
Top with ginger ale and dash the bitters over the top.

recipes.name: Irish Coffee
methodSteps: Warm a stemmed glass and dissolve the sugar in the coffee.
Add the whiskey.
Float lightly whipped cream on the back of a spoon.

recipes.name: Kir
methodSteps: Pour the crème de cassis into a chilled wine glass.
Top with the white wine and stir once.

recipes.name: Lemon Drop Martini
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled, sugar-rimmed cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Long Island Iced Tea
methodSteps: Build the five spirits, the lemon and the syrup over ice in a highball.
Top with cola.
Stir once and garnish with a lemon slice.

recipes.name: Mai-Tai
methodSteps: Shake the five with ice.
Pour into a lowball over crushed ice.
Garnish with mint and a spent lime shell.

recipes.name: Margarita
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass with a salted rim.

recipes.name: Mimosa
methodSteps: Pour the orange juice into a chilled flute.
Top slowly with the champagne and stir once.

recipes.name: Mint Julep
methodSteps: Put the mint and sugar in a julep cup and press them gently.
Fill with crushed ice and add the bourbon.
Stir until the cup frosts, and top with more ice.

recipes.name: Mojito
methodSteps: Press the mint, sugar and lime gently in a highball.
Add the rum and crushed ice, and stir.
Top with soda.

recipes.name: Moscow Mule
methodSteps: Fill a copper mug with ice.
Add the vodka and lime, then the ginger beer.
Stir once and garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.name: Pina Colada
methodSteps: Blend the three with crushed ice until smooth.
Pour into a chilled glass.
Garnish with a pineapple wedge.

recipes.name: Pisco Sour
methodSteps: Shake first without ice, to lift the white.
Shake again with ice.
Strain into a chilled glass and dash the bitters on the foam.

recipes.name: Sea Breeze
methodSteps: Build the three over ice in a highball.
Stir once and garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.name: Sex on the Beach
methodSteps: Build the vodka and schnapps over ice.
Add the orange juice, then the cranberry.
Stir once.

recipes.name: Singapore Sling
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a highball over ice.
Garnish with pineapple and a cherry.

recipes.name: Tequila Sunrise
methodSteps: Build the tequila and orange juice over ice.
Pour the grenadine slowly down the inside of the glass.
Do not stir: the colour is the drink.

recipes.name: Vesper
methodSteps: Shake the three hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.name: Bramble
methodSteps: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup with ice.
Pour into a lowball over crushed ice.
Drizzle the blackberry liqueur over the top so it runs down through the ice.

recipes.name: Canchanchara
methodSteps: Build the four over ice in a lowball.
Stir once.

recipes.name: Chartreuse Swizzle
methodSteps: Build the four over crushed ice in a highball.
Swizzle with a barspoon until the glass frosts.
Garnish with mint and grated nutmeg.

recipes.name: Dark 'N' Stormy
methodSteps: Fill a highball with ice and add the rum.
Top with ginger beer.
Squeeze the lime over the top and drop it in.

recipes.name: Espresso Martini
methodSteps: Shake everything hard with ice -- hard enough to build the foam.
Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Three coffee beans on the foam.

recipes.name: Fernandito
methodSteps: Fill a highball with ice.
Pour the Fernet, then the cola.
Stir once.

recipes.name: French Martini
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Gin Basil Smash
methodSteps: Press the basil gently in the shaker.
Shake everything with ice.
Double strain into a lowball over ice.

recipes.name: Grand Margarita
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Jungle Bird
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a lowball over ice.
Garnish with a pineapple wedge.

recipes.name: Naked and Famous
methodSteps: Shake the four in equal parts with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: New York Sour
methodSteps: Shake the whiskey, lemon, syrup and white with ice.
Strain into a lowball over ice.
Float the red wine on top: it is the drink's one flourish.

recipes.name: Old Cuban
methodSteps: Press the mint, then shake it with the rum, lime and syrup over ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Top with champagne and dash the bitters.

recipes.name: Paloma
methodSteps: Salt the rim of a highball and fill it with ice.
Add the tequila and lime.
Top with grapefruit soda and stir once.

recipes.name: Paper Plane
methodSteps: Shake the four in equal parts with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Penicillin
methodSteps: Shake the whisky, lemon, honey and ginger with ice.
Strain into a lowball over ice.
Float the peated whisky on top -- it is the part that makes it a Penicillin.

recipes.name: Pisco Punch
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a lowball over ice.

recipes.name: Porn Star Martini
methodSteps: Shake the vodka, liqueur, passion fruit and vanilla with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass and float half a passion fruit on top.
Serve the sparkling wine beside it, in its own glass.

recipes.name: Russian Spring Punch
methodSteps: Shake the first four with ice.
Strain into a highball over ice.
Top with sparkling wine.

recipes.name: South Side
methodSteps: Press the mint, then shake everything with ice.
Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Spritz
methodSteps: Fill a wine glass with ice.
Pour the prosecco, then the Aperol.
Add a splash of soda and stir once.

recipes.name: Suffering Bastard
methodSteps: Build the gin, cognac and lime over ice in a highball.
Top with ginger beer and dash the bitters.
Garnish with mint.

recipes.name: Tipperary
methodSteps: Stir the three over ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.

recipes.name: Tommy's Margarita
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a lowball over ice.
No orange liqueur, and no salt: the agave is the sweetener.

recipes.name: Trinidad Sour
methodSteps: Shake the four with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Yes: the bitters are the base.

recipes.name: Cardinale
methodSteps: Stir the three over ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a lemon zest.

recipes.name: Zombie
methodSteps: Blend everything with about 170 g of cracked ice, in short pulses.
Pour into a tall glass.
Garnish with mint.
The grapefruit and cinnamon together are Donn's Mix: two parts fresh yellow grapefruit to one part cinnamon syrup.

recipes.name: Rabo de Galo
methodSteps: Build the three over ice in a lowball.
Stir briefly.
Two drops of Angostura and an orange twist, both optional and both worth it.

recipes.name: Ve.N.To
methodSteps: Shake everything vigorously with ice.
Strain into a small tumbler over ice.
Garnish with lemon zest and white grapes.
The honey mix is made with chamomile infusion instead of water, and the cordial is chamomile: the flower is the drink.

recipes.name: Sherry Cobbler
methodSteps: Shake the sherries, the sugar and two quarter wheels each of orange and lemon with ice.
Strain into a julep cup packed with crushed ice.
Garnish with berries and a quarter wheel of each, and serve with straws.
Two named sherries, not "sherry": Amontillado and Palo Cortado, and the drink is built on the difference between them.

recipes.name: Spicy Fifty
methodSteps: Shake everything with ice.
Double strain into a chilled cocktail glass -- the double strain is what keeps the chilli out of the drink while leaving its heat in.
Garnish with a red chilli.

recipes.name: Don's Special Daiquiri
methodSteps: Blend everything with crushed ice for a few seconds.
Pour into a footed glass and top up with more crushed ice.
Garnish with half a passion fruit.

recipes.name: Missionary's Downfall
methodSteps: Blend everything with half a cup of crushed ice.
Pour into a large stemmed glass.
Garnish with a mint sprig and a slice of pineapple.
Ten mint leaves and three chunks of pineapple are blended *in*, not garnished on: this is a drink with a salad in it, and that is the recipe.

recipes.name: Three Dots and a Dash
methodSteps: Flash blend everything with about 12 ounces of crushed ice.
Pour into a footed glass and top up with crushed ice.
Garnish with three cherries and a rectangular chunk of pineapple.
The garnish is the name: three cherries and a dash of pineapple is Morse for V, which stood for Victory.

recipes.name: IBA Tiki
methodSteps: Muddle a thin slice of ginger in the shaker.
Add everything else and shake vigorously with ice.
Strain into a chilled tiki glass over pebbled ice.
Garnish with citrus and a slice of dried pineapple.
The two rums are a deep aged one and a smoky one; a single rum makes a good drink and not this one.

recipes.name: Illegal
methodSteps: Shake everything vigorously with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass, or serve it on the rocks in a clay mug.
No garnish.

recipes.name: Old Fashioned
methodSteps: Put the sugar in the glass with the bitters and a splash of water.
Muddle until it dissolves, add the whiskey, then fill the glass with ice.
Stir and garnish with orange peel and a cherry.

recipes.name: Whiskey Sour
methodSteps: Shake the whiskey, lemon juice and syrup with ice.
Strain into a chilled glass over fresh ice.
Garnish with a cherry and half an orange slice.

recipes.name: Sazerac
methodSteps: Rinse a chilled glass with the absinthe and turn it so the inside is coated.
Stir the cognac, sugar and bitters with ice in a second glass.
Strain into the rinsed glass and twist the lemon peel over the top.

recipes.name: Sidecar
methodSteps: Shake the three with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Serve straight away, with no garnish.

recipes.name: White Lady
methodSteps: Shake the gin, triple sec and lemon juice with ice.
Strain into a large chilled cocktail glass.
Serve with no garnish.

recipes.name: Stinger
methodSteps: Stir the cognac and crème de menthe with ice cubes.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
A mint leaf on top is optional.

recipes.name: Tuxedo
methodSteps: Stir the gin, vermouth, maraschino, absinthe and orange bitters with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with a cherry and a twist of lemon zest.

recipes.name: Vieux Carré
methodSteps: Stir the rye, cognac, vermouth, Bénédictine and bitters with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Garnish with orange zest and a maraschino cherry.

recipes.name: Rusty Nail
methodSteps: Pour the Scotch and Drambuie into the glass over ice.
Stir gently.
Twist a piece of lemon peel over the top.

recipes.name: Planter's Punch
methodSteps: Pour everything straight into the glass.
Fill it with ice and stir once.
Garnish with orange zest.

recipes.name: Porto Flip
methodSteps: Shake the brandy, port and egg yolk hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Grate nutmeg over the top.

recipes.name: Paradise
methodSteps: Shake the gin, apricot liqueur and orange juice with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Serve with no garnish.

recipes.name: Golden Dream
methodSteps: Shake the four with cracked ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Serve with no garnish.

recipes.name: Yellow Bird
methodSteps: Shake the four with ice.
Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
Serve with no garnish.

recipes.name: Ramos Gin Fizz
methodSteps: Shake everything except the soda water long and hard with ice.
Strain into a tall chilled glass and let the foam settle.
Top with soda water so the foam rises above the rim.

recipes.name: French press
methodSteps: Put the ground coffee in the jug and pour on water just off the boil.
Stir it once, put the lid on, and leave it four minutes.
Press the plunger down slowly and pour it out.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Moka pot
methodSteps: Fill the base with water up to the valve and put the ground coffee in the basket without pressing it.
Screw the two halves together and set it on a low flame.
Take it off as soon as it starts to hiss, and pour it at once.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Caffe americano
methodSteps: Pull the espresso into a cup.
Pour the hot water over it.
Stir it once so the crema settles back in.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Latte
methodSteps: Pull the espresso into a jug.
Steam the milk until it is glossy, then pour it in, holding the foam back with a spoon.
Spoon the foam on top.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Instant coffee
methodSteps: Put the instant coffee in the cup with the sugar.
Pour a little hot water on and stir it into a paste.
Add the rest of the water.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Vienna coffee
methodSteps: Pull the espresso into a tall glass.
Whip the cream until it just holds a peak.
Spoon it on top, and do not stir it in.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Vanilla milkshake
methodSteps: Put the milk, the ice cream and the vanilla in a blender.
Blend it until it is smooth and thick.
Pour it into a cold glass and serve it at once.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Hot cocoa
methodSteps: Stir the cocoa and the sugar together in the cup so no lumps form later.
Pour in a little hot milk and work it into a paste.
Add the rest of the milk and stir it until it steams.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Eggnog
methodSteps: Beat the egg yolk with the sugar until it is pale.
Add the milk and the cream and shake it with ice until it is cold.
Strain it into the glass and grate nutmeg over the top.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Sweet lassi
methodSteps: Put the yogurt, the milk and the sugar in a blender.
Blend it for half a minute, until it is loose and frothy.
Pour it over ice.
recipes.description: The weights and volumes below are a starting point, not a measurement this application can check.

recipes.name: Cream soda
methodSteps: Put the sugar in the bottom of the glass and add the ice.
Pour the soda water in and stir until the sugar has gone.
Float the cream on top, over the back of a spoon.
recipes.description: The two liquids have to be cold and the glass colder, or the cream will not float.

recipes.name: English tea with milk
methodSteps: Warm the pot, put the leaves in, and pour water just off the boil over them.
Leave it four minutes, then pour it into the cup.
Add the milk and the sugar.
recipes.description: Milk in first or last is a household argument, not a fact this application can settle.

recipes.name: Earl Grey milk tea
methodSteps: Steep the Earl Grey for three minutes rather than four: bergamot turns bitter before the tea does.
Warm the milk and pour it in.
Add the sugar and stir once.
recipes.description: Milk in first or last is a household argument, not a fact this application can settle.

recipes.name: Hong Kong milk tea
methodSteps: Steep a strong pot of black tea long enough that it reads as dark as coffee.
Pour it back and forth between two pots a few times to pull the astringency out.
Fill the cup two-thirds with the tea and top it with evaporated milk.
recipes.description: A target for your own kettle and your own scale; the application cannot see the cup.

recipes.name: Thai milk tea
methodSteps: Steep the tea strong, then strain it.
Stir the condensed milk in while the tea is still hot.
Fill a glass with ice, pour the tea over it, and float the evaporated milk on top.
recipes.description: A target for your own kettle and your own scale; the application cannot see the cup.

recipes.name: Masala chai
methodSteps: Boil the water with the crushed cardamom, the clove and the cinnamon for two minutes.
Add the tea and boil it another minute.
Pour the milk in and bring it back to a simmer, then strain it into the cup.
recipes.description: Crush the spices rather than grinding them; ground spice clouds the cup and turns it bitter.

recipes.name: Vietnamese iced coffee
methodSteps: Put the condensed milk in the bottom of the glass.
Brew a strong coffee and pour it over the milk while it is hot.
Fill the glass with ice and stir it up from the bottom.
recipes.description: The condensed milk is the sugar; adding more makes it a dessert.

recipes.name: Lemonade fizz
methodSteps: Fill a highball with ice.
Pour the lemonade in first.
Top it with the soda water and stir once.
recipes.description: Build it in the glass and keep everything cold; this is a drink that dies in a warm room.

recipes.name: Orange and grapefruit fizz
methodSteps: Pour the grapefruit juice into the glass over ice.
Add the orange soda slowly, down the side, so it keeps its gas.
Stir it once and serve it at once.
recipes.description: Build it in the glass and keep everything cold; this is a drink that dies in a warm room.

recipes.name: Pomegranate fizz
methodSteps: Pour the pomegranate juice over ice.
Top it with the soda water.
Stir it once, gently -- it stains anything it sits on.
recipes.description: Build it in the glass and keep everything cold; this is a drink that dies in a warm room.

recipes.name: Lychee cooler
methodSteps: Pour the lychee juice and the lime juice over ice.
Top it with the soda water.
Stir once; lychee is sweet enough that the lime is doing the work of keeping it drinkable.
recipes.description: Build it in the glass and keep everything cold; this is a drink that dies in a warm room.

recipes.name: Guava fizz
methodSteps: Pour the guava juice over ice.
Top it with the soda water.
Stir it once from the bottom, because guava settles.
recipes.description: Build it in the glass and keep everything cold; this is a drink that dies in a warm room.

recipes.name: Rose lemonade
methodSteps: Pour the lemonade over ice.
Add the rose water -- five millilitres is enough; more tastes of soap.
Stir it once and drink it cold.
recipes.description: The rose water is the one line here that can be overdone, and badly.

recipes.name: Peach iced tea
methodSteps: Steep the tea strong and let it cool completely -- hot tea poured on ice turns cloudy.
Muddle a quarter of a peach in the glass.
Pour the tea over it, add the sugar, and fill the glass with ice.
recipes.description: A target for your own kettle; the application cannot see the cup.

recipes.name: Green tea
methodSteps: Let the kettle rest for a minute after it boils; green tea scorched by boiling water is bitter.
Steep it for two minutes and no longer.
Pour it off the leaves.
recipes.description: A target for your own kettle; the application cannot see the cup.

recipes.name: Chocolate milk
methodSteps: Melt the chocolate with a spoonful of the milk over a low heat.
Stir it into the rest of the cold milk until it is even.
Pour it over ice, and add the sugar only if it needs it.
recipes.description: Chocolate on its own is not sweet; taste it before adding sugar.

recipes.name: Maple milk
methodSteps: Warm the milk without letting it boil.
Stir the maple syrup in off the heat.
Pour it into the cup and drink it while it is hot.
recipes.description: Serve it hot -- this is a winter drink, and cold milk with maple is not the same thing.

recipes.name: Iced coffee
methodSteps: Pull the espresso and let it cool completely.
Stir the sugar into the coffee while it is still warm.
Fill a glass with ice and pour the cold coffee over it.
recipes.description: Cool the coffee before it goes anywhere near ice; poured hot it turns bitter and thin.

recipes.name: Iced tea
methodSteps: Steep the tea strong and let it cool down completely.
Stir the sugar in while it is warm.
Pour it over ice, and do not add more water -- the ice will do it.
recipes.description: Cool the coffee before it goes anywhere near ice; poured hot it turns bitter and thin.

recipes.name: Lemonade
methodSteps: Squeeze the lemon and keep the peel out of the juice.
Shake the juice with the sugar and a little water until the sugar has gone.
Pour it over ice and top it up with the rest of the water.
recipes.description: A lemon held at room temperature gives more juice than one straight from the cold.

recipes.name: Orange juice
methodSteps: Squeeze the oranges and strain the pulp out if you want it clear.
Taste it before adding any sugar.
Pour it over ice and drink it at once.
recipes.description: Two oranges make one glass only if they are good ones; the sugar is there for the bad mornings.

recipes.name: Ginger ale
methodSteps: Grate the ginger and steep it in a little hot water for ten minutes.
Strain it and stir the sugar into the still-warm liquid.
Let it cool, then top it with the soda water over ice.
recipes.description: The ginger syrup keeps for a few days; the fizz does not, so it is added at the glass.

recipes.name: Iced cocoa
methodSteps: Make a paste of the cocoa and the sugar with a little cold milk.
Work the rest of the milk in, then chill it.
Pour it over ice and stir it once.
recipes.description: Cool the coffee before it goes anywhere near ice; poured hot it turns bitter and thin.

recipes.name: Egg cream
methodSteps: Melt the chocolate with a spoonful of the milk.
Put it in the bottom of a tall glass and pour the cold milk in on top.
Add the soda water last and stir it hard from the bottom, once.
recipes.description: The Brooklyn original is made with chocolate syrup. This is melted chocolate, which is thicker -- thin it with a spoonful of the milk before it goes in.

recipes.name: Coffee granita
methodSteps: Sweeten the coffee while it is hot, then let it cool.
Freeze it in a shallow tray and break it up with a fork every half hour.
Spoon the crystals into a glass; do not let it melt into a slush.
recipes.description: A fork and a shallow tray beat a machine here -- the crystals are the point of the drink.

recipes.name: Almond milk drink
methodSteps: Pour the almond syrup into the glass.
Add the cold milk and stir it from the bottom.
Fill the glass with ice and stir it once more.
recipes.description: Medieval cooks made this with ground almonds and water; the syrup is the short way to the same cup, and the difference is that the syrup is sweet already.

recipes.name: Strawberry cordial
methodSteps: Shake the strawberry syrup with the lemon juice and the water.
Pour it over ice.
Top it with a little more water and stir once.
recipes.description: A cordial is a syrup drink cut with water; the lemon is there because the syrup alone is flat.

recipes.name: Brown sugar ginger tea
methodSteps: Bruise the ginger with the flat of a knife and simmer it in the water for ten minutes.
Stir the brown sugar in and let it dissolve.
Strain it into the cup and drink it hot.
recipes.description: The ginger is bruised, not grated, when the tea is made in a pot -- grated ginger turns the cup cloudy and hot in the throat.

recipes.name: Cocoa tea
methodSteps: Stir the cocoa and the sugar together dry, so no lumps form.
Pour a little hot water on and work it into a paste.
Add the rest of the water and bring it just to the edge of a boil.
recipes.description: Cocoa was drunk with water for a century before anybody put milk in it.

recipes.name: Honey lemon
methodSteps: Squeeze the lemon and shake it with the honey syrup and a little water.
Pour it over ice.
Top it up with the rest of the water and stir once.
recipes.description: Honey does not dissolve in cold water; the syrup is why this one shakes rather than stirs.

recipes.name: Rose milk
methodSteps: Stir the rose water and the sugar into a little of the milk.
Add the rest of the milk and stir it until the sugar has gone.
Pour it over ice -- five millilitres of rose water is the whole line between a drink and a soap.
recipes.description: Rose water is easy to overdo and impossible to take back out.

recipes.name: Apple juice
methodSteps: Press the apples and strain the juice.
Taste it before adding anything; a good apple needs nothing.
Pour it over ice and drink it at once.
recipes.description: Pressed and drunk the same day; it browns within the hour and that is not a fault in the fruit.

recipes.name: Coconut water
methodSteps: Open the coconut and pour the water out through a strainer.
Add a squeeze of lime -- it is the one thing coconut water wants.
Pour it over ice.
recipes.description: Drunk straight from the nut in most of the places it grows; the glass is the only new part.

recipes.name: Lemon sorbet glass
methodSteps: Put two scoops of the sorbet in a cold glass.
Pour the soda water over it, slowly.
Serve it with a spoon and drink what melts.
recipes.description: Serve it in a glass with a spoon rather than in a bowl -- the difference between this and a dessert is width.

recipes.name: Usucha
methodSteps: Sift the matcha into the bowl so it does not clump.
Add the hot water -- not boiling -- and whisk it in quick straight strokes.
Drink it before the foam settles.
recipes.description: Thin tea, the everyday bowl; the thick one is a different drink and a different amount of leaf.

recipes.name: Houjicha
methodSteps: Put the roasted tea in the pot.
Pour water just off the boil over it and steep it for thirty seconds.
Pour it off at once -- it goes bitter quickly, and it is cheap enough to use a second time.
recipes.description: Roasted tea takes hotter water than green tea does, and much less time.

recipes.name: Sweet soy milk
methodSteps: Warm the soy milk without letting it boil.
Stir the sugar in off the heat.
Pour it into the cup and drink it warm, not hot.
recipes.description: Soy milk is older than any coffee on this list; the sugar is the part that makes it a treat.

recipes.name: Ristretto
methodSteps: Grind fine and dose as for a normal shot.
Stop the shot at about half the usual volume.
Drink it at once, while the crema is still there.
recipes.description: The same dose of coffee, stopped early or run long -- the difference is water, not beans.

recipes.name: Lungo
methodSteps: Dose as for a normal shot.
Run the water through for twice as long as usual.
Taste it before deciding it is too weak -- the bitterness arrives at the end.
recipes.description: The same dose of coffee, stopped early or run long -- the difference is water, not beans.

recipes.name: Shakerato
methodSteps: Pull a double espresso and sweeten it while it is hot.
Shake it hard with plenty of ice until the tin is cold through.
Strain it into a chilled glass without ice.
recipes.description: Shake it hard and pour it at once; the foam is the whole point and it does not keep.

recipes.name: Decaffeinated coffee
methodSteps: Treat it like any other coffee: water just off the boil, four minutes.
Pour it off the grounds rather than leaving them in the cup.
Drink it as it is, or with milk.
recipes.description: Decaffeinated coffee is 1903; the drink is as old as the process.

recipes.name: Grapefruit juice
methodSteps: Halve the grapefruit and press it, keeping the pith out of the glass.
Taste it; add sugar only if it is a bitter one.
Pour it over ice.
recipes.description: The grapefruit is a 18th-century crossing and the juice came with the Florida groves.

recipes.name: Tonic with lime
methodSteps: Fill a glass with ice and pour the tonic down the side of it.
Squeeze the lime in and drop the shell in after it.
Stir it once, and do not add sugar -- the tonic is already sweet.
recipes.description: Tonic was a medicine before it was a mixer, and it is drunk straight in the places that made it.

recipes.name: Espresso
methodSteps: Dose eighteen grams of ground coffee into the basket and level it.
Tamp it flat, lock the basket in, and start the shot.
Stop it at thirty-six millilitres.
recipes.description: The ratio is 1:2 -- eighteen grams in, thirty-six millilitres out. Everything else is the machine.

recipes.name: Filter brew
methodSteps: Rinse the filter and warm the pot.
Wet the grounds and wait thirty seconds.
Pour the rest in stages and let it drain.
recipes.description: The ratio is 1:15, and the water goes in stages; pouring it all at once is what makes a bitter cup.

recipes.name: Moka brew
methodSteps: Fill the base with water to the valve and the basket with grounds, unpressed.
Assemble it and set it on a low flame.
Take it off when it starts to hiss and pour it at once.
recipes.description: The water goes in the base and never touches the grounds until it is pushed up through them.

recipes.name: Cold brew
methodSteps: Put the grounds in a jar and cover them with cold water.
Leave it twelve hours in the refrigerator.
Strain it twice and keep it cold.
recipes.description: Cold water and time instead of heat: ten to one, twelve hours, and strain it after.

recipes.name: Whipped cream
methodSteps: Chill the bowl and the cream.
Whip it until it holds a soft peak.
Stop there -- a few seconds more and it separates.
recipes.description: Cold cream, cold bowl, and stop before it turns to butter.

recipes.name: Lemon sorbet
methodSteps: Boil the sugar and water into a syrup and let it cool.
Add the lemon juice once the syrup is cold.
Freeze it, breaking it up every half hour.
recipes.description: Sugar and water first, lemon last; acid added early dulls the colour.

recipes.name: Ice cream
methodSteps: Warm the milk, cream and sugar and pour them over the yolks, whisking.
Cook it gently until it coats a spoon, then chill it completely.
Churn it, and freeze it hard before serving.
recipes.description: Custard base, chilled, then churned. The yolks are what make it hold together.

recipes.name: Coffee ice cream
methodSteps: Soften the ice cream enough to stir, but not enough to melt it.
Fold the espresso through it -- a little at a time, tasting as it goes in.
Freeze it again for an hour before it is served.
recipes.description: A base made out of another base: this one opens the ice cream beneath it.

recipes.name: Affogato
methodSteps: Put two scoops of the coffee ice cream in a cold glass.
Pull the espresso and pour it over while it is still hot.
Serve it at once, with a spoon.
recipes.description: The Italian word means drowned, and that is the whole instruction.

recipes.name: Ice cream soda
methodSteps: Put the syrup in the bottom of the glass.
Pour the soda water down the side and do not stir it hard.
Float two scoops of the ice cream on top and serve it with a spoon.
recipes.description: Two finished things -- the syrup and the ice cream -- used as ingredients, which is the whole point of the tree.

recipes.name: Coffee cream
methodSteps: Whip the cream to a soft peak.
Add the espresso a spoonful at a time, folding rather than stirring.
Stop as soon as it holds -- more coffee and it collapses.
recipes.description: A base whose ingredients are themselves bases: the whipped cream and the espresso both arrive with their own methods.

recipes.name: Café liégeois
methodSteps: Put two scoops of the coffee ice cream in a cold glass.
Pour the cold espresso over them.
Spoon the coffee cream on top and serve it at once, with a long spoon.
recipes.description: Three finished things in one glass, and each of them opens to its own method.

recipes.name: Sage tea
methodSteps: Put a few sage leaves in the cup and pour water just off the boil over them.
Steep it five minutes and no longer -- sage turns bitter quickly.
Strain it and add honey if you want it.
recipes.description: A herb tea, and the honey is optional -- sage on its own is a taste people either want or do not.

recipes.name: Blackberry cordial
methodSteps: Crush the blackberries with the sugar and leave them an hour.
Strain the juice out and add the lemon to it.
Shake it with a little water and pour it over ice.
recipes.description: A cordial is a syrup cut with water; the lemon keeps it from tasting like jam.

recipes.name: Coffee with milk
methodSteps: Warm the milk without letting it boil.
Pour the filter coffee in first, then the milk on top of it.
Stir it once and drink it hot.
recipes.description: The milk goes in warm, and the coffee should be stronger than you would drink it alone.

recipes.name: Apple juice fizz
methodSteps: Pour the apple juice over ice.
Top it with the soda water, down the side of the glass.
Stir it once and drink it before the fizz goes.
recipes.description: Apple juice already tastes of apple; the soda is there for the fizz and nothing else.

recipes.name: Mint lemonade
methodSteps: Bruise the mint between your hands and put it in the shaker.
Add the lemon juice, the sugar and a little water, and shake it hard.
Pour it over ice and top it up with the rest of the water.
recipes.description: Bruise the mint rather than chopping it -- chopped mint bleeds and turns the drink green-brown.

recipes.name: Honey ginger
methodSteps: Bruise the ginger and simmer it in the water for ten minutes.
Take it off the heat and stir the honey syrup in.
Strain it into the cup and drink it hot.
recipes.description: Hot, and drunk before it cools; the honey goes in off the heat.

recipes.name: Turkish coffee
methodSteps: Put the coffee, the sugar and the cold water in the pot and stir it once.
Set it on a low heat and do not stir it again.
When the foam rises, take it off and pour it slowly, foam first.
recipes.description: Ground to powder, water cold, and the foam is the whole judgement -- it is made once and not stirred.

recipes.name: Café de olla
methodSteps: Boil the water with the cinnamon and the brown sugar until the sugar has gone.
Add the coffee, take it off the heat and put a lid on it.
Leave it five minutes, then strain it into the cups.
recipes.description: The clay pot is not decoration: it holds the heat differently and takes the cinnamon with it.

recipes.name: Egg coffee
methodSteps: Beat the egg with the condensed milk until it is a pale cream.
Pull a small strong coffee and pour it into the cup.
Spoon the cream on top and serve it with a spoon, hot.
recipes.description: The yolk and the condensed milk are beaten to a cream that sits on the coffee rather than in it.

recipes.name: Greek frappé
methodSteps: Shake the instant coffee, the sugar and a little cold water until it is all foam.
Pour it over ice in a tall glass.
Top it with the rest of the water and add milk if you want the white one.
recipes.description: Instant coffee is required -- the foam only happens with the soluble kind, which is why this is 1957.
